notes.title: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy”
notes.intro: Paul discusses God’s choice of Jacob over Esau and his sovereign mercy. Readers have long debated what this means for individual salvation.

views.label: God chooses individuals for salvation (unconditional election)
views.summary: Reformed Christians read the chapter as teaching that God freely chooses those he will save, not based on anything they do.
views.source: Westminster Confession 3; Canons of Dort, First Head

views.label: God’s choice concerns his plan for peoples and roles
views.summary: Many read Romans 9 as about God’s plan for Israel and the nations, not the eternal destiny of individuals.

views.label: God’s foreknowledge and human freedom work together
views.summary: Catholic and Orthodox Christians affirm God’s sovereignty and human free cooperation with grace.
views.source: Catechism of the Catholic Church 600, 2002; St John Chrysostom, Homilies on Romans

notes.common: All agree salvation is God’s mercy and not earned.
